name: NE5532 / NE5532A / SA5532 / SE5532 (dual low-noise bipolar; incl. NJM5532, KA5532, BA15532, RC5532)
tagline: The 1979 Signetics dual that became the pro-audio benchmark: 5 nV/rtHz, 600 ohm drive, cheap. Douglas Self's reference part; Soomal calls it the 'king of op-amps'.
technology: Bipolar, internally compensated (unity-gain stable) dual; the dual version of the NE5534 core. Legacy parts (Signetics/Philips, onsemi, TI up to SLOS075J) use an NPN input pair with anti-parallel input-protection diodes and a class-AB output specified into 600 ohm. TI's current die (documented from SLOS075K, Dec 2025) is a redesign on a newer process after the move from SFAB Sherman (150 mm) to RFAB Richardson. A TI E2E thread (Jun 2026) says NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 now share one die, and summaries describe it as RC4580-derived with no input diodes. Input-stage polarity is disputed: Gearspace says PNP, the E2E-thread summary says NPN.
manufacturers: Texas Instruments (second source; datasheet SLOS075, still active)
ON Semiconductor / onsemi (NE5532, NE5532A, SA5532, SE5532, SE5532A; datasheet NE5532/D)
JRC / New JRC / Nisshinbo Micro Devices (NJM5532)

reputation.summary: The reference pro-audio op-amp since 1979 and the stock part that op-amp rolls are judged against. Douglas Self uses it as the benchmark in Small Signal Audio Design and argues bad reports come from misuse. NwAvGuy's 2011 measurements put it alongside far pricier parts. Soomal (China) calls it '号称运放之皇' ('reputed king of op-amps') and uses it as a benchmark tier ('4558 < 5532/4580'). Japanese reviewer nabe treats it as the baseline 'normal audio op-amp' (rank B). Vintage Signetics and Philips stock has a following in Japan and China, and junker-life preferred Signetics/Philips by ear over TI and JRC. These are subjective reports.
sonic_descriptors: neutral / clean, transparent at line level when used correctly (Self)
soft, warm mid-bass with slower transients and less treble resolution than modern parts (Soomal RNHP review)
retro / vintage flavour ('复古的味道', Soomal)
flat or plain next to boutique parts (op-amp rollers)
typical_uses: mixing consoles and pro line stages driving 600 ohm
CD player and DAC I/V and output stages
powered speakers (e.g. Soomal's 鹂之声 启明星)
caveats: TI parts on the new die (documented from SLOS075K, Dec 2025, though forums say shipments began earlier) are rated 5 V/us slew and ±18 V absolute maximum, and the 600 ohm drive specs are gone. Designs on ±18 to ±22 V rails can be overstressed. Production boards failed QA after the change (Scott Dorsey, via Headphonesty).
The new TI die reportedly drops the input-protection diodes and halves HBM ESD (2 kV to 1 kV).
Needs split rails of at least about ±5 V. The output is not rail-to-rail (common-mode range ±12 V on ±15 V).
Quiescent current is several mA per package, so it runs warm in dense or small builds.
Bipolar input bias current (hundreds of nA) causes DC offset with high source impedance. It is not a drop-in for FET-input sockets that rely on low bias current.
Legacy parts have anti-parallel input-protection diodes, so they are unsuitable as comparators or with large differential inputs.
Brands differ. Douglas Self reportedly found TI parts noisier with higher HF THD than Fairchild/onsemi (forum report, not primary-source verified). JRC NJM5532 is described as looser.
Counterfeit and remarked 'NOS Signetics/Philips' parts are common on marketplaces.

silicon_changes.when: Process-migration PCN 20231114002.1 dated 15 Nov 2023. Production moved from SFAB Sherman (150 mm) to RFAB Richardson around 2024 (Gearspace: 'K version - 2024>'). Datasheet SLOS075 went from Rev J (Jan 2015) to Rev K (Dec 2025). Datasheet PCN 20260429001.1 is dated 30 Apr 2026 (first ship 29 Jul 2026). TI confirmed the die merge on E2E, and Hackaday reported it on 3 Jun 2026.
silicon_changes.identification: Orderable part numbers are unchanged and no date-code cut-over has been published. The silicon change came under PCN 20231114002.1 (15 Nov 2023; lists NE5532DR and SA5532ADR, and per TI E2E 1299478 NE5532AP, with through-hole in group 1 and SMD in group 2). The datasheet only caught up in SLOS075K (Dec 2025; datasheet PCN 20260429001.1), so 2024-or-later lots may be new silicon even when sold against Rev J. SLOS075K is a single datasheet ('NE5532x, SA5532x') covering all four grades. Two bench checks: legacy parts have back-to-back diodes across the inputs and the new die reportedly has none (unpowered diode check between IN+ and IN-); and slew rate is about 5 V/µs on the new die versus 9 V/µs on the legacy one. TI E2E thread 1294367 (late 2023) asks for a PCN on an NE5532DR 'symbolization format' (marking) change, which may be a visual clue (unconfirmed).
silicon_changes.summary: TI replaced the NE5532/NE5532A/SA5532/SA5532A silicon with a different design on a newer RFAB process without changing the part numbers. TI confirmed on E2E that NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 are now the same die. Rich Cabot (Audio Precision co-founder), quoted by Hackaday, said 'they just relabeled a 4580'. Reporting describes the die as RC4580-type, with NPN inputs and a complementary output stage. According to Hackaday and search summaries, the November 2023 PCN noted the new process, the ±22 to ±18 V supply reduction and the 2 kV to 1 kV ESD reduction, yet stated no datasheet change and no customer impact. The datasheet was updated only in December 2025 (Rev K), and the datasheet PCN followed in April 2026. Hackaday calls the result incompatible even with the original Signetics NE5532, and other vendors' NE5532s keep the original specs.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Full-power bandwidth at 10 V peak falls from about 143 kHz to about 80 kHz (computed from the slew rate), leaving less HF THD margin at high output level. Drive into 600 ohm and other heavy loads is no longer guaranteed. Consoles and powered speakers on ±18 to ±22 V rails, often unregulated, can exceed the new absolute maximum. Without the input diodes, circuits that relied on them for differential-input clamping lose that protection. The higher GBW and different input stage can change stability and HF behaviour in legacy layouts. Production boards failed QA after the TI parts were swapped in (Scott Dorsey, via Headphonesty).
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: high - same part number but lower voltage rating, slower slew, halved ESD, no input diodes and deleted load-drive guarantees. Not a drop-in for legacy ±18 to ±22 V or 600 ohm designs.
silicon_changes.verification: Merged three reports of one event (main pass, sweep 'PCN 20231114002.1' entry, sweep 'Rev K' entry). Searches confirmed PCN 20231114002.1 lists NE5532DR/SA5532ADR (process migration plus MLA assembly site; 22 to 18 V; 2 to 1 kV ESD; 'no datasheet change'). TI E2E 1299478 confirms NE5532AP is in the same PCN. The E2E 1652528 title and Hackaday's Cabot quote and 15 Nov 2023 PCN date were also confirmed.

silicon_changes.summary: Each vendor built the same generic number on its own die. Forum reports: Douglas Self found TI noisier, with higher HF THD, than Fairchild/onsemi. Original Signetics parts are reportedly up to about 10 dB quieter with about 20 dB lower distortion than modern TI. JRC NJM5532 is called 'looser', and Japanese opinion puts TI closest to Signetics. Soomal (2009) says a speaker's noise floor fell when it switched from JRC5532 to TI5532, but the crossover was retuned in the same revision, so the op-amp's share is unclear. Since 2024, TI's NE5532 is additionally a different, RC4580-type die (see the TI die-redesign entry).
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Possible differences in noise, HF THD and bias current between brands. Evidence is mostly forum measurements and listening reports.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - pin- and function-compatible across legacy vendors; parameter spread only (post-2024 TI parts excepted, see the die-redesign entry).

counterfeit_notes: Remarked fakes are common on marketplaces, especially 'NOS Signetics/Philips' parts (vintage stock sells for over 100 RMB in China, which motivates relabelling). Elektroda shows a fake NE5532 decapped next to a genuine one (https://www.elektroda.com/rtvforum/topic3386559.html), and TI E2E has an 'NE5532: Genuine or fake?' thread (https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1474706/ne5532-genuine-or-fake). Discovery notes also mention relabelled LM741-class dies (diyAudio fake-AD797/LM741 thread). To spot fakes: a genuine 5532 draws several mA per package, far above LM358/741-class parts. It should drive 600 ohm cleanly and slew about 9 V/us (legacy) or 5 V/us (new TI). Compare the marking font and logo against known date codes, and buy from authorized distributors. A genuine new TI part now slews at only 5 V/us and has no input diodes, so neither test alone proves a fake.

revision_chain_notes:
I used all 14 WebSearch calls. A few results were near misses, and some gaps remain.

TI SLOS075 (oldest to newest): original Nov 1979, A (Sep 1990), B (missing), C (Jun 2000), D, E and F (all missing), G (Jun 2002), H (May 2004), I (Apr 2009), J (Jan 2015), K (Dec 2025). No search result showed a B, D, E or F header. One search summary claimed 'SLOS075B is the TI revision reference', but no source supported it, so I did not record it. New copies of known revisions: a Rev. H copy at ccrma.stanford.edu (PDF title '(Rev. H)'); a probable Rev. J copy on Mouser (2015 'Product Folder' layout); a probable Rev. I copy at televideo.ws ('1FEATURES' layout). The Octopart SA5532DR copy, alldatasheet 27245, 27248 and 785133, and datasheetcatalog show no revision. alldatasheet 27248 (NE5532P, 10 pages, upper-case 1990 to 2004 style title) is the most likely place to find one of the missing B, D, E or F. Fetch it to check.

Philips/Signetics: 1997 Sep 29 Product specification (radiolux.com.ua, probably also alldatasheet 17968), then 2001 Aug 03 Product data, which 'Supersedes data of 1997 Sep 29' (ben.cz). Missing: any pre-1997 Signetics or Philips edition (the 1979 original and any 1980s or 1994 data-book editions), any NXP re-issue after 2006, and the Philips semiconductors.philips.com/acrobat file names. Datasheet Archive has only listing pages.

onsemi NE5532/D: Rev. 1 (Mar 2006), then Rev. 2 (Sep 2013). No Rev. 0, Rev. 3 or later was found. The current download URL (onsemi.com/download/data-sheet/pdf/ne5532-d.pdf) was not confirmed, so fetch it to see whether it is still Rev. 2. alldatasheet 175241 shows no revision.

Fairchild: KA5532 Rev. 1.0.1 (©2002, Farnell) is new. NE5532 Rev. 1.0.2 (©2009) was already known. Missing: KA5532 editions from before 2002 or under the Samsung brand, and any other Fairchild NE5532 revisions.

JRC/Nisshinbo NJM5532: Ver.2020-03-31 (Mouser NJM5532_E) is new. Older JRC and JRC5532 editions exist on alldatasheet (7453, 7458) but their dates were not shown. Any later Nisshinbo Ver. date is missing.

ST: no ST NE5532 datasheet or DocID turned up, including in a search restricted to st.com. ST may never have published one, so its status is unconfirmed.

Archive seeds: the focus.ti.com symlink URLs and the onsemi pub_link/Collateral/NE5532-D.PDF URL follow each vendor's known legacy URL pattern and did not appear in any search result. Use them only for Wayback lookups. The ben.cz and onsemi download URLs did appear in results.
